conventions.convention: The spin label includes zero; r = 2s + 1, the state space is L²(R³; Cʳ), and inner products are linear in the first argument.
Spatial rotations act by U(R)f(x) = f(R⁻¹x). The cover used with Pauli axes is ρ(W) = C⁻¹ρ₀(W)C, with C having rows (0,0,-1), (0,-1,0), (-1,0,0); thus ρ(Aᵢ(t)) = Rᵢ(t).
Orbital angular momentum has rotation flow exp(-itLᵢ/ℏ); spin is Sᵢ = ℏJᵢ; total angular momentum is Lᵢ + Sᵢ on D(Lᵢ). Their assigned unit is J s.

The magnetic coupling is HZ = H₀ - γs Σᵢ Bᵢ(Q)Sᵢ, with real bounded measurable B, real γs in s⁻¹ T⁻¹, and domain W²,²(R³; Cʳ). It is an adopted effective interaction, without a Maxwell/source realization.
ω = γs Bz is signed; transverse spin expectations rotate through angle -ωt.

Orbital preparations use R ∈ Cc∞((0,∞)) and homogeneous harmonic polynomials h_lm, not merely their sphere restrictions. Normalization requires R ≠ 0; the squared-angular-momentum assertion is a quadratic-form identity on these vectors.

The Stern–Gerlach force uses bounded C¹ Bz with bounded derivative and initial vectors in D(HZ²). The splitting calculation additionally assumes exact marginal containment throughout [0,τ]; normalized sector means are defined only for positive sector weights.
The spin-half singlet is the normalized antisymmetric vector; uniqueness means uniqueness of a unit kernel vector up to phase, while the full kernel is its complex line.
The two-level energy difference ΔE = γℏBz is explicitly signed; the truncation replaces the spatial free operator by the scalar E₀I as an additional toy assumption.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC and countable choice. For self-adjoint A on a nonzero complex Hilbert space and bounded self-adjoint B commuting with every exp(isA), A+B is self-adjoint on D(A), the flows commute, and exp(isA)exp(isB) = exp(is(A+B)), whose infinitesimal generator is i(A+B) on exactly D(A).

Under AC and countable choice, Us(W) = U(ρ(W))Ms(W) is a strongly continuous unitary SU(2) representation; ρ(Aᵢ(t)) = Rᵢ(t); Lᵢ and Sᵢ strongly commute; Jᵢ = Lᵢ+Sᵢ is self-adjoint on D(Lᵢ), with Us(Aᵢ(t)) = exp(-itJᵢ/ℏ). Position and momentum conjugations use maximal directional domains.
For the declared massive spin-s model, assign (Lᵢ, J s), (Sᵢ, J s), and (Lᵢ+Sᵢ, J s) as orbital, spin, and total angular momentum sharp observables, with the total operator on D(Lᵢ).

Under countable choice, the restrictions (1/ℏ)Lᵢ to each degree-l sphere block Vl are unitarily equivalent to the spin-l matrices; ΣᵢLᵢ²F = ℏ²l(l+1)F on Vl and ΣᵢLᵢ²F = ℏ²AF on the finite harmonic span.
Adopt μ = γs S and HZ = H₀ - Σᵢγs Bᵢ(Q)Sᵢ on W²,²(R³; Cʳ), for real γs and a real bounded measurable prescribed static field profile.

Under the stated postulates, sharp-observable assignments, AC and countable choice, Sn has spectrum ℏ{-s,-s+1,…,s} and fibrewise projection Born weights; S² = ℏ²s(s+1)I; for spin half, Pn,± = (I ± n·σ)/2 and the probabilities are (1 ± ⟨(n·σ)ψ,ψ⟩)/2.

For the declared internal spin factors, total spin has the orthogonal Clebsch–Gordan decomposition with j = |s-t|, |s-t|+1,…,s+t, each once; for two spin-half factors, the displayed singlet spans the one-dimensional zero-Casimir kernel and is the unique unit kernel vector up to phase.

concerns.concern: Definition (c) says “S_± are not self-adjoint” without excluding the permitted spin label s = 0. For s = 0 all spin matrices vanish, so both ladder operators are the zero self-adjoint operator. The finite-spin supplier explicitly includes this case.

The first Remark says the sum “requires the strong commutation of the two summands for self-adjointness of the sum.” This necessity claim is false: bounded self-adjoint perturbations preserve self-adjointness without commutation. The product-flow lemma's adjoint proof establishes this directly, and its own Remark explicitly says the flow hypothesis is unnecessary for clause (a). Strong commutation is used for the product-flow identification.

Postulate (ii) reads the Zeeman flow through P4 and explicitly cites post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics, but that ID is absent from deps and dependency_roles. This is an actual formulation prerequisite for the physical evolution reading.

The Statement and F3 attribute the two-spin tensor-product representation Ds ⊗ Dt to P6 clause (ii). The current P6 clause defines each Ds and a separately assigned spatial representation tensor Ds; it does not explicitly assign the rotation action of two internal spin factors. P1 supplies the composite state space. The matrix decomposition remains valid, but the asserted physical representation assignment needs an explicit local adoption or a faithful supplier attribution.

The page calls ΔE = ℏω a “gap”. Its example explicitly defines ΔE as a signed level difference, with γ and Bz unrestricted in sign. A nonnegative energy gap would be |ℏω|; the summary should preserve the example's signed-difference terminology.

alerts.finding: Clause (f) says “the parameter a of a translation has the unit of length u_H”. Clause (a) and def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution use u_H for the energy unit. The translation parameter has a length unit, but this symbol is inconsistent with its defined energy meaning.

Proof 3.1 invokes “J²u = λ(λ+1)u from step 2.1”, while step 2.1 explicitly establishes the corresponding quadratic-form value and J₊J₋u = 2λu. The required vector equality follows immediately from J² = J₋J₊ + Jz² + Jz and J₊u = 0, but that one-line inference is unstated before its use.

seams_checked.note: Rotation action, orbital generator signs, maximal directional conjugate domains, and conditional law/moment conservation are preserved.
Strong commutation means commuting spectral projections; the bounded Borel-calculus use retains this hypothesis.
The quaternion cover is explicitly transported by C; the page does not identify its literal imaginary-basis matrix with the Pauli-axis cover.
SO(3) is used with its stated matrix and Euclidean-topology conventions.
The mathematical cross-product identity is used without importing classical central-force dynamics or physical interpretation.
Component-valued L² space, componentwise position/momentum domains and fibrewise internal actions retain the supplier's scope.
Sphere generators, harmonic polynomial representatives, normalization and finite spin/tensor decomposition are used at their stated domains and block scopes.
Units and postulate neutrality are preserved, but the two-spin theorem attributes Ds ⊗ Dt to current P6(ii), which does not explicitly assign that two-internal-factor action; see concern.
Sharp observable assignments include units; spectral atom laws and domain-qualified moments are preserved.
Preparations are density operators or normalized nonzero rays; no zero vector is treated as a preparation.
Hilbert tensor construction and scalar free/bounded-potential self-adjointness are used with explicit componentwise amplification.
Evolution and density transport use the stated spectral flow and sign convention. The magnetic postulate omits its directly cited P4 dependency metadata.
The force transport retains bounded C¹ coefficients, bounded derivative, D(HZ²), and the preparation-time restriction for the constant-gradient specialization.
Examples remain conditional model calculations with SI units and no invented measured parameters or sampling claims.
Product preparations and componentwise operators retain the massive spin-s space; Zeeman operator expectations require the free domain.
Directional probabilities are normalized Born projection weights; model probabilities are distinguished from observed frequencies.
Product spinors are unit vectors and sector normalization is restricted to positive weights.
Low harmonics preserve the associated-polynomial phase convention, sphere normalization and degree-zero case.
The full-space unitary flow is separated from domain-restricted Hamiltonian expectations and the explicitly adopted finite toy truncation.
The A-page summary makes no stronger angular-momentum claim; explicit directional-spin uses occur on its examples companion.

Singlet and mixture consumers use the finite internal Pauli projections. Their finite-factor law is the same elementary matrix calculation as the fibrewise supplier, with local physical assignments stated.
The declared arrangement uses the Pauli projection formula and separately declares joint sign measurements; it does not infer an apparatus realization from spin spectra.
Worked product-mixture probabilities specialize the directional projection formula to the two basis spinors.
Current F3 correctly states uniqueness of a unit singlet up to phase and uses the kernel line and triplet dimension.
The Zeeman multiplet example explicitly restricts to the finite spin-one internal factor, where eigenspaces are one-dimensional, and scales the precession frequency by λ.
